question: Which of the following is responsible for the dispersion of white light through a glass prism?

options.text: Different colours of light travel at different speeds in glass.
White light contains only one colour.
Different colours of light travel at the same speed in glass.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Different colours of light travel at different speeds in glass.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Dispersion of white light** occurs when white light passes through a glass prism. It splits into its constituent colors, forming a spectrum (VIBGYOR: Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red).
 
• This phenomenon is due to the fact that **different colors of light travel at different speeds in glass**. Each color has a different wavelength, and the refractive index of glass varies with the wavelength of light.
 
• **Violet light** bends the most, while **red light** bends the least. This is because violet has the shortest wavelength, and red has the longest wavelength among the visible spectrum.
 
• The separation of white light into its constituent colors is referred to as **dispersion**.
